Customer (Nicole Fraser): I need to close my account at the old address and set up payments for the new one.
Agent (Sipho Nkosi): Hi Nicole Fraser, Sipho Nkosi here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Nicole Fraser): Do I need to be home for anyone to come out, or can this be done remotely?

Customer (Nicole Fraser): What's the actual turnaround time between the stop and the start?
Agent (Sipho Nkosi): What date do you need the stop to take effect?
Customer (Nicole Fraser): The last day of the month. That's when we hand the keys back.
Agent (Sipho Nkosi): Would you like pre-authorized payments set up at the new address?
Customer (Nicole Fraser): Yes, same bank as now.

Agent (Sipho Nkosi): Possibly for a day or two. The new meter needs a technician to turn it on, and the earliest slot is a few days out.
Agent (Sipho Nkosi): To recap: the stop is booked, the new meter needs a technician visit, and you're on the priority list for an earlier slot.
Customer (Nicole Fraser): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sipho Nkosi): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Kevin Campbell): Can you explain how the equalization plan works out my monthly amount?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Hi Kevin Campbell, Nomsa Khumalo here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Kevin Campbell): If the point of this plan is predictable payments, why does it keep moving?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Understood. Let me pull up the account and look at the charges before I say anything.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Kevin Campbell): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Kevin Campbell): This is the third time this year my equalized amount has changed on me.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): When did you first join the equalization plan?
Customer (Kevin Campbell): About two years ago, when we moved in.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Did you get a notice before the amount changed?
Customer (Kevin Campbell): No. I found out when the payment came out.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Has anything changed at home, like a new appliance or more people?
Customer (Kevin Campbell): We had a baby, so the heat's been on more.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the equalization plan's 12-month usage average and the reconciliation adjustment that triggered the change.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): The plan averages your last twelve months of usage and is reviewed at month six. If usage runs higher than the estimate, the difference is added.
Customer (Kevin Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): The plan recalculates twice a year against your rolling usage average, and this adjustment reflects higher usage than last year's estimate — I've set up an email alert so you'll get advance notice before the next recalculation instead of finding out on the bill.
Customer (Kevin Campbell): Will it change again without warning?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): The next review is in six months, and you'll get an email two weeks before it.
Customer (Kevin Campbell): And the catch-up amount?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): I've spread it over your remaining months so there's no lump sum.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap: the catch-up is spread over the rest of the plan year, and you'll get an email two weeks before the next review.
Customer (Kevin Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Sipho van der Merwe): It shouldn't. Most of this month's jump is colder weather, not the rate change.
Agent (Sipho van der Merwe): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Customer (Amanda Scott): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
